nodes.name: NF pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A piece of NF (2.0 cm×6.0 cm) was subjected to ultrasonic cleaning for 30 min to remove the possible oxides in 1.0 M HCl, and then washed for 15 min by using C2H6O and DI, respectively.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, the NF was subjected to ultrasonic cleaning for 30 min to remove the possible oxides in 1.0 M HCl, and then washed for 15 min by using C2H6O and DI, respectively.

nodes.name: IrNi-FeNi3/NF hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: IrCl3·xH2O and FeCl3 were dissolved in an aqueous solution consisting of 30 mL C2H6O. Subsequently, the pretreated NF substrate was immersed into the solution. After gentle stirring for 10 min, the mixture was added into a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and maintained for 12 h at 180°C. When it cooled down to room temperature, the obtained IrNi-FeNi3/NF was cleaned for several times by using DI and C2H6O, respectively, and then dried in a vacuum for lasting 12 h at 80°C.

nodes.name: Pt/C/NF preparation
nodes.procedure: 5.0 mg 20 wt.% Pt/C or 40 wt.% IrO2/C were dissolved in 1.0 mL solution, respectively, which was made up of 20.0 μL 5.0 wt.% Nafion solution and 0.98 mL C2H6O. Then it was placed in ultrasonic for about 15 min. Finally, 10.0 μL solution was dropped on the surface of NF to form Pt/C/NF and IrO2/C/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: IrNi/NF shows main peak at 41.39° between Ir(111) and Ni(111), indicating IrNi alloy formation. IrNi-FeNi₃/NF shows additional peaks at 44.277°, 51.532° and 75.867° corresponding to FeNi₃(111), (200) and (220) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a, the main peak of IrNi/NF at 41.39° is between the (111) plane of the standard diffraction peak of Ir(PDF#87-0715) and the (111) plane of Ni(PDF#70-0989) at 40.66° and 44.6°, respectively, exhibiting the formation of IrNi alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir 4f XPS of IrNi-FeNi₃/NF shows Ir⁰ (68.79%) at 60.70 eV (4f₇/₂) and 63.70 eV (4f₅/₂), Ir⁴⁺ (31.21%) at 61.51 and 64.51 eV due to partial air oxidation, with ~0.2 eV positive shift vs IrNi/NF indicating electronic interaction between IrNi and FeNi₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peak of Ir 4f spectra at 60.70 eV corresponds to Ir 4f₇/₂ of Ir⁰ . The peak at 63.70 eV is the Ir 4f₅/₂ of Ir⁰ . Other peaks at 61.51 and 64.51 eV are ascribing to Ir⁴⁺ ... The content of Ir⁰ and Ir⁴⁺ are 68.79 % and 31.21 % ... compared with IrNi/NF, the Ir 4f peaks in IrNi-FeNi₃/NF display a positive shift of ∼0.2 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p spectra shows peaks at 706.8, 711.65, 716.18 eV (Fe 2p₃/₂ of Fe, Fe²⁺, satellite) and 720, 724.85, 729.38 eV (Fe 2p₁/₂ of Fe, Fe²⁺, satellite), indicating Fe³⁺ precursor reduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2c shows the Fe 2p spectra, the peaks located at 706.8, 711.65 and 716.18 eV are assigned to Fe 2p₃/₂ of Fe, Fe²⁺ and satellite peak, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p spectra shows Ni⁰ at 852.64 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂) and 869.94 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂), Ni²⁺ at 855.76 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂) and 873.06 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂) due to partial air oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p XPS spectra (Fig. 2d), the peaks of 852.64 and 869.94 eV correspond to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂ of Ni⁰, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show 2D nanosheets structure of IrNi-FeNi₃/NF hybrid. SEM-EDS confirms even distribution of Ir, Fe, Ni on nanosheet surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, SEM images show the 2D nanosheets structure of IrNi-FeNi₃/NF hybrid (Fig. S1), and the SEM-EDS images indicate the Ir, Fe and Ni are evenly distributed on the surfaces of nanosheets (Fig. S2).
